summary: A pathological kidney whose tissue has been replaced by countless cysts of varying size, the gross picture of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. The kidney keeps its bean shape, with the renal pelvis and ureter leaving from the hilum. Oriented as a left kidney seen from the front, as in the creator's thumbnail.
clinical: Mostly caused by mutations in PKD1 (polycystin-1, chromosome 16) or PKD2 (polycystin-2, chromosome 4). It presents in adulthood with hypertension, flank pain, haematuria, cyst infection or bleeding, and large palpable kidneys. Features outside the kidney include liver cysts, berry aneurysms of the circle of Willis and mitral valve prolapse.

Ultrasound shows both kidneys enlarged and full of cysts, and age-specific cyst counts are used when there is a family history. Kidney function declines as the cysts grow, and many patients need dialysis or a transplant in middle age. Tolvaptan, a vasopressin V2-receptor antagonist, can slow cyst growth in rapidly progressing disease.

SubTool-1.name: Polycystic kidney
SubTool-1.description: An enlarged kidney whose tissue is replaced by innumerable fluid-filled cysts of different sizes. The dark cysts suggest old bleeding into them. Large, irregular cysts bulging from the surface are typical of the adult dominant form, which affects both kidneys. The recessive childhood form instead gives smooth, enlarged kidneys with tiny, radially arranged cysts.

SubTool-3.name: Renal pelvis and ureter
SubTool-3.description: The funnel-shaped renal pelvis sits in the renal sinus at the hilum and narrows into the ureter, which carries urine down to the bladder. Kidney stones are more common in polycystic kidney disease.

notes: The file has the hilum facing backwards (-z). It is rotated 90 degrees about the vertical so the hilum faces the viewer's left, which matches the creator's thumbnail and reads as a left kidney seen from the front; the creator does not say which side it is. The creator's description says only 'polycystic kidney'. The ADPKD framing is my reading of the gross appearance (large kidney, cysts of mixed size, some dark/haemorrhagic). The model is a surface shell, so a cut shows no interior.
